structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E048. The tip is still E036 (5.314 s; seeds 0–2 at 0.7532).

1. Noise. Commit 60645dd has read 0.7532, 0.7525, 0.7497 and 0.7544 on seeds 0–2 across rebuilds, so the SD is about 0.2 pp around a population mean of about 0.7527. A neutral change clears 0.753 about 40–45% of the time. Bands for neutral changes should be ±0.3 pp. Time reproduces to about ±0.03 s.

2. A mechanism nobody has stated, read from the code. `muon_update` applies no weight decay at all, and it renormalizes every filter to norm √C_out on each step. Filter wd has therefore always been inert. E016's ×0.5 wd gain, and every later wd result, acts only through the SGD groups (BN biases at 64× lr, whitening bias, head). So wd on BN biases is a live knob, and the E022 comparison (×0.25 on the SGD groups) was effectively a global wd dose test. It came out flat to negative, so the optimum is near ×0.5. This settles H1.5.4 by reading the code.

3. Freezing with an annealed LR is close to free once the stem has seen 32 px (E028, E036, E046). An early freeze is not (E037 at 60% lost). Changing the objective or the averaging costs 0.2–0.5 pp (E025, E030, E032, E044). Frozen blocks save 1.5–2× their FLOP share (E028, E046: about 10 ms per frozen step), because they also drop BN/GELU backward, per-parameter Muon NS kernels and the next group's dgrad. Time is about conv compute plus a ~30% memory-bound and optimizer tail.

4. Steps versus pixels. Early low resolution at a fixed step count is nearly free (E026, E033). Removing steps costs about the same as the dial (E040, E041, E031, E048). Adding steps buys at about the dial rate (E045). The dial runs at about 1.2–1.8 s/pp. Loss-based selection (E048: −6% time, −0.14 pp on seeds 0–2) is about as good as the dial, not better.

5. Hidden systems waste. Each epoch loop augments, interpolates and permutes all 50k images at every resolution it touches, including the 10th loop, which runs only about 7 steps. Total steps are ceil(9.25×25) = 232, so the last pass mostly wastes augmentation and interpolation. That is part of E047's 135 ms of non-step work. Making it lazy (augment only the slices that are used) saves about 1–2% with identical math. Per-batch copy into static cudagraph inputs is another ~1%.

6. Strategy. Stack freezes and buy accuracy back with epochs. Judge systems levers on time plus a same-build check of per-seed bit-identity. The PCIe judge adds about 5–10% to absolute times, and the ranking probably holds.

Unsure:
- whether ReLU costs CIFAR-100 accuracy (prior −0.2 to −0.4 pp);
- whether Inductor saves a bool mask or the fp16 output for ReLU's backward;
- E046's 20-seed delta;
- whether the 13–32 vs 3–12 gap is winner's curse or seed-set difficulty.

forecasts.reason: E046's 5.079 s scaled by about +2.6% steps gives about 5.21 s, right at the 2% bar. The accuracy delta against E036 will sit within 20-seed noise (SE about 0.06 pp), so the 0.03 pp criterion can't be resolved cleanly.
With identical math, about 50–100 ms of the 135 ms non-step work is removable, including the wasted full-dataset augment and interpolate on the short 10th epoch. Accuracy is only rebuild noise.

The fused kernels are bound by BN statistics and residual bytes, and ReLU's backward probably saves an fp16 tensor, so the time saving is about 1.5%, not ≥3%. GELU→ReLU likely costs about 0.2–0.3 pp on CIFAR-100.

cruxes: In the same build on seeds 13–32, how many pp does E046's group-2 freeze alone lose against E036? Under about 0.05 pp makes freeze plus top-up a clean dominance; about 0.15 pp means the cascade only matches the dial.
How much of E047's 135 ms of non-step work is the wasted full-dataset augment and interpolate in the short final epoch loop plus the static-input copies, i.e. removable with bit-identical math?

Muon applies no wd and renormalizes filters, so every wd result is really a BN-bias/head wd result. Is there an untested dose between ×0.25 and ×0.5 on the SGD groups (or a different wd on the head alone) worth ≥0.15 pp, which would fund a further epoch trim?
